predecessors.name: Mataram Kingdom
predecessors.text: the East Javanese remnant of Mataram, whose capital Wwatan was destroyed in 1006; Airlangga 'rallied support from officials and regents that were loyal to the former Isyana dynasty'

successors.name: Kediri Kingdom
successors.text: the western half: 'Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms which were inherited by his two sons; Janggala and Kediri'

successors.name: Janggala
successors.text: the north-eastern half, read from Cliopatria's 1046 shapes

ledger.x: 1019: Airlangga founds the Kingdom of Kahuripan in East Java.

c. 1028: Kahuripan grows beyond its core into Central Java. 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali.' The page gives no year; 1028 is Cliopatria's. Mataram, whose land this was, had fallen in 1006/1016, so no state is named as the loser.

c. 1028: Bali is brought under Kahuripan. The page's wording is 'extended his kingdom to... Bali' and gives no year. The Airlangga page says he was 'born 1002 in Bali'; neither page says whether Bali was held directly or as an ally or vassal.
1037: Airlangga moves the capital from Watan Mas to Kahuripan.
1045: Airlangga divides his kingdom and abdicates.
1045: the second kingdom of the partition, Janggala.
1045: Bali drops out with the partition.
1045: Kahuripan ends in the partition into Janggala and Kediri.

wars.name: Wurawari rebellion against Mataram
wars.outcome: The Mataram capital Wwatan was destroyed and Airlangga went into exile; in 1019 he rallied the loyal officials and founded Kahuripan.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the extent is only 'from Pasuruan in the east to Madiun in the west' and, undated, Central Java and Bali.
